scenes.text: How to sell *AI vector files* on Etsy, step by step

scenes.title: Step 1: *pick a lane*
lines: SVG cut files for Cricut users, logo templates, sticker sheets. One niche: teachers, nurses, dog groomers.
Search Etsy for 'svg bundle' and read the top ten listings before you make anything.

scenes.title: Step 2: *make it*
lines: Ideogram Vector 1.0 (Oct 22). Prompt: 'Floral monogram frame, single color, clean closed paths, no text.'
Open the SVG in Inkscape (free) or Canva. Delete stray points, name the layers, test a cut if you own a machine.

scenes.title: Step 3: *prove it*
lines: Etsy's Oct 22 AI rules: state your creative role, disclose the AI, show a real preview.
Cut one on vinyl and photograph it. That photo is your listing image.

scenes.title: Step 4: *list it*
lines: Claude prompt: 'Write an Etsy title, 13 tags and a description for this SVG bundle. Shopper language, no AI hype.'
Bundle 10 to 20 files. Bundles outsell singles.

scenes.title: The *math*
lines: A $6 bundle: Etsy keeps 20 cents listing, 39 cents transaction, 43 cents processing. You keep about $5.
Twenty sales a week is roughly $400 a month. Sales, not a promise.

scenes.title: *Tested*, not hyped
lines: Vector 1.0 costs 13 to 32 cents a file through the API; app plans from $15 a month.
Never sell a logo that copies a brand. Sources: Ideogram, Oct 22; Etsy Seller Handbook, Oct 22, 2026.
